description:
fz      %{:a => 1, :b => 2}
    elixir  %{a: 1, b: 2}

Elixir uses the `key: value` shorthand when every key is an atom that needs no
quoting, and falls back to `%{"x" => 1}` form otherwise. fz always uses the
arrow form.

Blocks oracle fixtures that print any atom-keyed map -- which is most maps a
program builds by hand. Note the ITERATION ORDER of an atom-keyed map cannot
match Elixir either (separate ticket), so a fixture printing one needs both
fixed before it can have an oracle; a fixture printing a BINARY-keyed map needs
only this one.

DONE = a map renders exactly as Elixir renders it for atom keys, mixed keys,
and keys needing quotes, with a fixture whose golden comes from the oracle.
title: [BUG] dbg renders a map's atom keys as :a => rather than Elixir's a:
